examples.ko: 급행을 타면 삼십 분 만에 도착해요.
examples.en: If you take the express, you arrive in thirty minutes.
The express does not stop at small stations.
Where do I transfer to the express?
I bought an express train ticket in advance.

examples.ko: 급행이 오기 전에 한 번 더 확인했어요.
examples.en: I checked once more before the express came.
There were almost no seats on the express.

explain: 빨리 가는 열차나 버스는 '급행', 모든 역에 서는 것은 '완행'이나 '일반'이라고 해요. 서울 지하철 9호선에는 급행이 있어요.
explain_en: A train or bus that goes fast is a '급행', and one that stops at every station is a '완행' or '일반'. Seoul subway Line 9 has an express service.

examples.en: I like popular music more than classical.
We learned the history of popular music in class.
K-pop is also a part of Korean popular music.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 대중음악에 큰 영향을 줬어요.
examples.en: That singer had a big influence on popular music.

examples.ko: 대중음악은 시대에 따라 유행이 많이 변해요.
examples.en: Trends in popular music change a lot with the times.

examples.ko: 대중음악과 클래식을 둘 다 즐겨 들어요.
examples.en: I enjoy listening to both popular music and classical.

explain: 클래식 같은 음악과 비교하거나 수업, 기사에서 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서 한국 대중음악은 '가요'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when contrasting with classical music, or in classes and articles. In daily talk, Korean popular music is also called '가요'.

examples.en: This outfit looks too dull.

examples.ko: 멋없는 발표라서 아무도 박수를 안 쳤어요.
examples.en: It was such a dull presentation that nobody clapped.
I'm really sorry for saying it so tactlessly.
The movie's ending was lame, so I was disappointed.
Please don't think the present is boring.
So what if it's not stylish? It's fine as long as it's comfortable.

explain: 반대말은 '멋있다'예요. '재미없다'는 흥미가 없다는 뜻이고, '멋없다'는 세련되지 않았거나 분위기가 없다는 느낌이에요. 사람에게 직접 말하면 기분 나쁘게 들릴 수 있으니 조심해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '멋있다'. '재미없다' means not interesting, while '멋없다' suggests unstylish or lacking charm. Saying it directly to a person can sound rude, so be careful.

examples.ko: 발표할 때 몸동작을 크게 하면 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: If you make big body movements during a presentation, you stand out.
We couldn't communicate in words, so I explained with gestures.
The child's movements are very cute.
In dance class, every single movement matters.

examples.ko: 나라마다 몸동작의 뜻이 다를 수 있어요.
examples.en: The meaning of a gesture can differ from country to country.

examples.ko: 강아지의 몸동작을 보면 기분을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tell a dog's mood by its body movements.

explain: '몸짓'과 뜻이 가까워요. 손만 움직일 때는 '손짓'이라고 해요. 운동이나 춤에서 몸을 움직이는 방법을 말할 때도 쓰고, '크게 하다', '따라 하다'와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is close in meaning to '몸짓'. When only the hands move, you say '손짓'. It is also used for how the body moves in exercise or dance, and it goes well with '크게 하다' and '따라 하다'.

examples.ko: 회의에서 나온 생각이 더 발전되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope the idea from the meeting develops further.

examples.ko: 작은 모임이 큰 단체로 발전될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: A small group could grow into a big organization.
A small idea developed into a big business.
It's fun to see the story develop little by little.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 관계가 친구에서 연인으로 발전되고 있어요.
examples.en: Their relationship is developing from friends into a couple.
Be careful that the talk doesn't turn into a fight.

explain: '한국이 발전했어요'처럼 스스로 좋아질 때는 '발전하다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '발전되다'는 아이디어, 관계, 상황이 다음 단계로 이어질 때 어울려요. 'A가 B로 발전되다'처럼 '-(으)로'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: When something improves by itself, as in 한국이 발전했어요, 발전하다 is much more natural. 발전되다 fits an idea, relationship, or situation moving on to a next stage. It is used with -(으)로, as in A가 B로 발전되다.

dis.h: progress to a better, more advanced state

p.n: 발달되다 stresses natural growth or maturing rather than improvement.

examples.en: I met a friend who works at a magazine company.

examples.ko: 저는 대학 졸업 후 잡지사에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: After graduating from university, I joined a magazine company.

examples.ko: 이 잡지사는 매달 새 책을 내요.
examples.en: This magazine company puts out a new issue every month.

examples.ko: 잡지사가 제 사진을 쓰고 싶다고 연락했어요.
examples.en: A magazine company contacted me and said they want to use my photo.
A reporter from a big magazine company came to the school.
I mailed the letter for the magazine company at the post office.

explain: '-사'는 회사를 뜻해서 신문을 만드는 곳은 '신문사', 책을 만드는 곳은 '출판사'라고 해요. 잡지를 만드는 회사는 잡지사예요. '잡지사에 다니다', '잡지사에서 일하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '-사' means company, so a company making newspapers is a '신문사' and one making books is a '출판사'. A company making magazines is a 잡지사. You say '잡지사에 다니다' or '잡지사에서 일하다'.

examples.en: I got a pearl necklace as a birthday gift.
Pearls form inside shellfish.
The white glow of the pearl is beautiful.

examples.ko: 이 반지에는 작은 진주가 박혀 있어요.
examples.en: A small pearl is set in this ring.
I opened the shell and there was a pearl.
I bought pearls as a wedding present.

explain: '진주'는 경상남도에 있는 도시 이름이기도 해요. 보석은 '진주 목걸이', '진주 귀걸이'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 자주 써요.
explain_en: 진주 is also the name of a city in South Gyeongsang Province. The gem is often placed before another noun, as in 진주 목걸이 and 진주 귀걸이.

examples.ko: 이 책은 실제 이야기가 아니라 픽션이에요.
examples.en: This book is fiction, not a true story.
I enjoy reading nonfiction more than fiction.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 픽션이지만 실제 사건에서 아이디어를 얻었어요.
examples.en: That movie is fiction, but it took its idea from a real event.
I picked a novel from the fiction corner of the bookstore.
Children grow their imagination by reading fiction.

examples.ko: 픽션에서는 작가가 이야기를 마음대로 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: In fiction, the author can make up the story freely.

explain: 반대말은 '논픽션'이에요. '소설'과 비슷하지만 영화, 드라마, 만화까지 넓게 가리킬 수 있어요.
explain_en: Its opposite is nonfiction. It is similar to the word for a novel, but it can also cover movies, dramas, and comics.
